rich_narrative.summary: Ta'leef Collective is a California-based organization <cite id="5">founded in 2005</cite> that focuses on providing a welcoming space for Muslims, particularly converts and those seeking a healthy understanding of Islam. The organization operates several core initiatives, including <cite id="5">Convert Care, Inheritors, and the Ta'leef Re-entry program</cite> for formerly incarcerated individuals. While the charity provides unique social and spiritual services, its financial profile presents a balanced mix of operational strengths and significant efficiency gaps. In FY2024, Ta'leef reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $1,397,233</cite>, representing a <cite id="3">three-year compound annual growth rate of 22.2%</cite>. However, the organization currently holds a <cite id="2">40/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, largely due to its spending structure. A neutral evaluation of the charity reveals a high-touch service model that results in a <cite id="2">program expense ratio of 11.7%</cite>, which is significantly below the 75% industry benchmark. This indicates that a large portion of funds is directed toward administrative and overhead costs rather than direct program delivery. Despite these financial concerns, the organization maintains <cite id="2">5.2 months of working capital</cite>, providing a level of short-term financial resilience. Ta'leef is <cite id="1">zakat-eligible</cite> and serves specific categories including the poor (fuqara) and those whose hearts are to be reconciled (muallaf).
